correctness.rationale: For a binary linear word, k universal subsequence coverage iff there are k disjoint adjacent unequal pairs (greedy minimal alphabet-covering arches). For n=2k+1 a cyclic rotation has such pairs exactly when the unequal-edge subgraph of the odd cycle has matching number k. Equal-adjacency edges break the cycle into paths; matching size=(n-E)/2, where E is number of even-length unequal paths. Hence exact condition E=1. Counting odd r=2s+1 equal edges and weak compositions gives L=(2k+1)2^k. Each admitted word has multiplicities k and k+1, so is primitive, giving 2^k necklaces. A prescribed dihedral reflection fixes 2^(floor(k/2)+1) admissible words and Burnside yields 2^(k-1)+2^floor(k/2) bracelets. Independent exhaustive checker verified edge parity, arch universality, and orbit counts for every k=1..7, with direct subsequence coverage for k<=5; infinity follows from matching and Burnside, not finite enumeration.
